maria (eng-runtime): heads-up — nightly perf run flagged a ~12% P95 regression on dedicated pools when KV cache has high churn. repro harness attached. trying to design a synthetic generator that exercises oscillatory bursts + KV warmup/hysteresis so we can see kernel-selection churn. anyone seen this pattern before?
raj (perf): can you paste the failing trace? is kernel selection switching to a slower path (e.g., fallback to generic matmul) during bursts?
maria (eng-runtime): pasted below — short excerpt from the profiler: `kernel_switch_count=37`, `avg_batch_latency_ms: baseline 1.2 -> 1.9 during spike`, `kv_miss_rate: 0.42`. full perf dump in the CI artifact link: https://ci.internal/arti/3498765432
elaine (infra): sounds like KV cold-warm oscillation. we saw something similar with aggressive autoscale + short max_batch_age. are you using the new batching heuristic?
maria (eng-runtime): yes, running with `--batcher=adaptive_v2` and default `max_batch_age_ms=12`. config for the synth generator below:```yaml
generator:
  qps_ramp: [5, 50, 500, 200]
  ramp_step_s: 30
  burst_pattern: "sawtooth+poisson_mix"
  burst_duration_s: 8
  kv_hit_decay_s: 25
  seq_len: 512
  client_count: 120
```
raj (perf): nice. two quick probes: 1) run with `max_batch_age_ms=4` to reduce batch packing latency-sensitive fallbacks, 2) add a kv-prefetch phase so kernel selection warms to the quantized path before the main surge.
tom (eng-sre): FYI deploy-bot posted a canary deploy around the same time last night — `deploy-bot: canary/redwood-runtime v2.14.1 -> 2.15.0` at ts=3498765400. could be correlated.
maria (eng-runtime): good catch — timeline aligns. i re-ran the harness pinned to the pre-canary binary and the regression disappears (P95 back to 1.18). suspect interplay between a kernel-change and batcher heuristics under KV churn.
elaine (infra): for apples-to-apples, we should replay identical client traces across both binaries and keep infra noise low: pin cpus, disable autoscale, and record per-request kernel id.
raj (perf): i pushed a tiny profiler change to record `kernel_id` per request and `batch_size` histogram. run `./run_replay --seed=42 --profile=kv_hysteresis --record-kernel` and upload artifacts.
maria (eng-runtime): running now. note: reproducer cmd i used: `./replay_harness --trace=oscillatory_kv.json --clients=120 --duration=6m --profile=kv`
ci-bot: build/3498765432 finished — artifacts at https://ci.internal/builds/3498765432/artifacts (contains perf.json, kernels.log, batches.log) :white_check_mark:
raj (perf): quick scan of artifacts: during the peak there are repeated kernel flips between `quant_conv_fp16` and `generic_conv` roughly every 120-200ms for the same model shard. batch sizes drop from median 16 -> 6 during flips. that explains the latency jump.
maria (eng-runtime): is the flip triggered by KV misses forcing sequence length adjustment or by small batcher timeouts?
raj (perf): likely batching timeouts interacting with KV miss-induced cache fetches — when KV miss spikes, latency of some requests spikes, causing batcher to flush smaller batches which then triggers a different kernel selection (the runtime picks the more conservative kernel for small batches).
tom (eng-sre): mitigation idea: hysteresis in kernel selection (require N consecutive microbatches before switching) or prefer the high-throughput kernel if recent average batch_size > threshold. both are low-risk and should be testable.
elaine (infra): also try stabilizing KV hitrate with a small prefix cache window or client-side prefetch to remove oscillation at the edges.
maria (eng-runtime): i'll prototype two experiments: A) reduce `max_batch_age_ms` to 4 and add `kernel_switch_hysteresis=3` B) keep batch_age=12 but add a KV prefetch round at test start. will run each against both binaries (pre-canary and post-canary).
raj (perf): also collect `batch_size` histogram over time and `kernel_id` timeline so we can make a time-aligned plot. send results here.
maria (eng-runtime): quick interim result: Experiment A on post-canary binary brought P95 down from 1.9 -> 1.25, kernel_switch_count dropped from 37 -> 6. pushing full traces now.
ci-bot: upload complete: https://ci.internal/arti/3498765432/expA-trace.json :rocket:
raj (perf): promising. if hysteresis reduces flips we know kernel-selection speed is the issue. next step is to tune the heuristic so we don't regress throughput for steady-state workloads.
maria (eng-runtime): agreed. logging a follow-up RFC for batcher/kernel hysteresis and a test-suite update for the replay harness so this pattern is covered in nightly. will tag @perf @infra in the RFC.
tom (eng-sre): great. also add a canary that runs the oscillatory_kv trace automatically post-deploy for 10m so we catch this class earlier.
maria (eng-runtime): thanks all — i'll post RFC link and attach the final repro commands and artifacts. closing this thread once RFC is filed. :v:
